# Tracing — PHP (beta)

<!-- @generated by grpc-dc codegen. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Dependency-free W3C Trace Context propagation for this 
runtime. The wire contract is in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) 
(Tracing); this page covers the language-level API. A 
runnable multi-service example (client -> callee -> 
downstream) is in [`../examples/tracing/`](../examples/tracing/).

## Enabling

Register an observer with `Status::setTracer(tracer)`. The observer receives 
`onStart`/`onEnd` callbacks with kind (`client`/`server`), 
method, trace/span ids, terminal status, and span duration 
in milliseconds. With no observer registered, tracing is 
dormant: no `traceparent` header is written and no ids are 
minted.

The protoc option `trace=off|hooks` only controls stub 
convenience: `hooks` re-exports the registrar from generated 
stubs and may bake a `trace_methods` filter. The runtime 
capability itself is always present and dormant. Sampling 
and export (OTLP or otherwise) are the application's 
problem — see the `tracing_demo` and `otlp_tracer` examples.

## Starting a trace (client-initiated)

A client call with no parent starts a root span 
automatically. To group several calls (and local work) 
under one workflow span, create a root with `Status::newTraceContext(kind, method)`, 
bind it as the parent of your calls, and end it when the 
workflow completes.

## Joining a trace (callee making outbound calls)

While a handler runs, its server span context is available as `$ctx->traceContext`. 
Parent outbound calls with `Channel::withTraceContext(ctx)`; the runtime then 
writes the outbound `traceparent` for you — child client 
span, downstream server span, one shared trace id. Explicit 
`traceparent` call metadata always wins over the bound or 
ambient context.

## Sampled flags

An upstream `traceparent` ending in `-00` is honored: the 
context still propagates downstream, but no spans are 
recorded. `-01` (and locally started spans) record 
normally. `tracestate` and `baggage` ride as ordinary 
metadata.
